The system is out of order - the give-way rules apply
Prepare to stop - a steady red light is coming shortly
sku-024.f: Sign/marking 1094 "Red stop flashing signal" (Sign Regulations § 24, the individual signals). Road users must not pass the signal. The stop must be made at the stop line or at a safe distance before the signal. The red stop flashing signal shows one or two alternately flashing red lights.

fb-001.s: On which side should overtaking normally take place?
a: On the left side
On the right side
On the side where there is the most space
On either side when the stretch is straight with a clear view
fb-001.f: Overtaking must take place on the left (Traffic Rules § 12 no. 1). The exceptions are few and precise: among others, when the vehicle in front is turning left or clearly preparing to - then the overtaking must be done on the right. The most important exception: when the car in front is turning left or clearly preparing a left turn, you pass on the right.

a: Overtaking motor vehicles with more than two wheels
All passing, including of cyclists and pedestrians
Overtaking heavy vehicles over 3,500 kg
Overtaking motor vehicles, including two-wheeled motorcycles and mopeds
fb-009.f: Sign 334 prohibits overtaking motor vehicles with more than two wheels (sign regulations § 8). Two-wheelers (bicycle, moped, motorcycle) may thus still be passed when otherwise safe and legal. The ban applies until cancellation sign 336.

vo-002.s: What does a solid yellow line in the middle of the road mean?
a: The line must not be crossed or touched - overtaking across it is prohibited
Overtaking is allowed when you have good visibility and it is clear
The line is advisory - it only shows where the middle of the road is
The line must not be crossed - but touching it with a wheel is allowed
vo-002.f: A barrier line (1004) must not be crossed or touched. A yellow barrier line is placed where overtaking across the line is dangerous - short sight lines, hilltops, bends (sign regulations § 22). Violations bring a fine and penalty points, because the consequence is a head-on collision.

sku-026.s: The yellow light is flashing over the road at a pedestrian crossing. What does it mean?
a: The pedestrian crossing is closed - drive past without stopping
You have a duty to give way to pedestrians only while the light is flashing
The signal system at the junction is out of operation
Show particular attentiveness and care
sku-026.f: Sign/marking 1098 "Yellow flashing signal" (Sign Regulations § 24, the individual signals). The signal indicates that road users must show particular attentiveness and care.

pf-003.s: Two lanes in the same direction merge into one (the lane ends). What applies?
a: The merging rule - you adjust speed and enter the lane alternately
Drivers in the ending lane must give way as in an ordinary lane change
You must move into the continuing lane well before the merging point
Whoever is a car length ahead has the right to merge first
pf-003.f: When the number of ordinary lanes in the same direction is reduced, the usual lane-change duty to give way does NOT apply - instead speeds must be mutually adjusted so drivers can continue alternately ("zipper merge", traffic rules § 8 no. 1 second paragraph). Use both lanes all the way to the merging point.

sp-003.s: Where is there a stopping ban, not just a parking ban?
a: In a blind bend, in a tunnel, on a hilltop and other places with poor visibility
In a blind bend, in a tunnel and in front of the entrance to a parking garage
At passing places, along their entire widened stretch
On a priority road where the speed limit is above 50 km/h
sp-003.f: The stopping ban (traffic rules § 17 no. 1) covers the most dangerous places: blind bends, tunnels, hilltops and other places with poor visibility - as well as pedestrian crossings, motorways and bus lanes, among others. The three other options are places with a PARKING ban (§ 17 nos. 2 and 3), where a short stop for loading/unloading is allowed.

Oncoming traffic must give way
Priority road
sko-021.f: Sign 214 "Oncoming traffic must give way" (Sign Regulations § 6, the individual give-way and priority signs). The sign indicates that oncoming traffic is ordered to give way by sign 212 "Give way to oncoming traffic".

sku-004.s: What does a yellow line with long dashes and short gaps mean?
a: Shows that the sight line is too short for normal overtaking
Must not be crossed or touched
Separates an ordinary lane from bus lanes and other special lanes
Marks the outer edge of the carriageway
sku-004.f: Sign/marking 1002 "Warning line" (Sign Regulations § 22, the individual lines and symbols). A yellow warning line indicates that the sight line ahead is too short for normal overtaking. A white warning line indicates danger when changing lanes. The line may be crossed, but only when you have unusually good visibility - it warns that overtaking is normally unsafe here.

sku-010.s: What does the wide white line across the carriageway mean?
a: Shows where you must stop when a stop is mandated
Shows the point where the duty to give way begins
Warns that a speed hump is coming soon
Shows the routing of the lane through the junction
sku-010.f: Sign/marking 1020 "Stop line" (Sign Regulations § 22, the individual lines and symbols). The line indicates where vehicles must stop when an official traffic sign or traffic light signal mandates a stop.

sku-011.s: What do the white triangles pointing towards you before the junction mean?
a: Shows where you must stop when a stop is mandated
Shows the routing of the lane through the junction
Marks a restricted area you may not drive on
Shows the point where the duty to give way begins
sku-011.f: Sign/marking 1022 "Give-way line" (Sign Regulations § 22, the individual lines and symbols). The line shows the place where the duty to give way takes effect.

sku-012.s: What does the area of wide white stripes across the carriageway mean?
a: The pedestrian crossing rules apply, even without a crossing sign
Crossing place for cyclists
The pedestrian crossing rules apply only where the crossing sign is put up
Shows where you must stop when a stop is mandated
sku-012.f: Sign/marking 1024 "Pedestrian crossing" (Sign Regulations § 22, the individual lines and symbols). The marking indicates that the traffic rules' provisions on pedestrian crossings apply even if sign 516 "Pedestrian crossing" is not put up.

sku-014.s: What does the white box with a P painted at the roadside mean?
a: Marks a restricted area you may not drive on
Indicates the vehicle must stand within the marking
Marks a space for disabled people with a parking permit
Marks a bus stop where stopping is prohibited
sku-014.f: Sign/marking 1028 "Parking bay" (Sign Regulations § 22, the individual lines and symbols). A parked vehicle must be placed within the marked bay. One or more electric and hydrogen-powered motor vehicles may nevertheless park across the bay's lengthwise direction if all the wheels are within the bay and the overhang beyond the bay does not exceed 40 centimetres on each side.

sko-041.s: Which sign has this meaning: "Zone where you may not leave an e-scooter"
a: Speed limit zone for small electric vehicles
Zone with a parking ban for small electric vehicles
Zone with a use ban for small electric vehicles
End of speed limit zone for small electric vehicles
sko-041.f: Sign 377 "Zone with a parking ban for small electric vehicles" (Sign Regulations § 8, the individual prohibition signs). The sign marks the boundary of an area where parking a small electric vehicle is prohibited. It applies until cancelled by sign 379 "End of zone with a parking ban for small electric vehicles". Within the area, deviating provisions on parking or stopping may be set; in those places the zone sign's provisions do not apply.

sko-020.s: Which sign has this meaning: "Do not enter the narrow stretch if it would obstruct vehicles coming towards you"
a: Give way
Oncoming traffic must give way
Give way to oncoming traffic
End of priority road
sko-020.f: Sign 212 "Give way to oncoming traffic" (Sign Regulations § 6, the individual give-way and priority signs). The sign prohibits entering a narrow stretch of road if doing so would obstruct oncoming traffic.

pf-011.s: Is it allowed to drive a car on the road shoulder?
a: Yes - in a queue the shoulder can be used as an extra lane
No - the car must drive in the carriageway, not on the shoulder
No - the shoulder may only be used by buses and taxis in rush hour
Yes, when the queue is at a standstill and you are taking the next exit
pf-011.f: Vehicles must be driven on the carriageway and kept well within the lane (traffic rules § 5 no. 1). Only bicycles/vehicles that are not motor vehicles - and small electric vehicles - may use the right shoulder. A car on the shoulder is reserved for emergencies.

sp-007.s: Is it allowed to stop in a bus lane to drop off a passenger?
a: Yes - a short stop for boarding and alighting is allowed also in bus lanes
No - stopping in a bus lane is prohibited, also for boarding and alighting
No - boarding and alighting must happen in a lay-by outside the lane
Yes - for electric cars and others who may legally use the lane
sp-007.f: It is prohibited to stop in a bus lane, carpool lane or cycle lane - the only exception is a bus or tram at a stop (traffic rules § 17 no. 1). The ban covers even short boarding/alighting, and regardless of vehicle type.

sp-008.s: Can you park partly on the pavement when the street is narrow?
a: Yes - with two wheels on the pavement, as long as pedestrians can get past
No - only vans loading or unloading may stand on the pavement
No - it is prohibited to stop wholly or partly on a pavement
Yes - outside the centre, where pedestrian traffic on the pavement is light
sp-008.f: It is prohibited to stop wholly or PARTLY on a pavement, footpath or cycle path (traffic rules § 17 no. 1). "Two wheels on the pavement" is thus illegal even for a short stop - the pavement belongs to the pedestrians.

ly-003.s: Can fog lights be used together with the dipped beam on a car?
a: Yes - together they give the best possible view in darkness and precipitation
No - fog lights replace the dipped beam in fog and precipitation
Yes, but only in dense fog where visibility is under 50 metres
No - fog lights may only be used together with the main beam
ly-003.f: Cornering/fog lights cannot be used together with the dipped beam (traffic rules § 15 no. 5) - fog lights are used instead of the dipped beam when visibility is reduced. (Motorcycles have a separate daylight exception.) Auxiliary lights must generally only be used for their purpose. Technically it is often possible to switch on both - but the rules do not allow it: fog lights are an alternative to the dipped beam, not an addition.

ra-010.s: What requirements apply to private practice driving with a car (class B)?
a: The pupil must have turned 16 and taken the basic traffic course, and the car must have an L-plate and an extra mirror
The pupil must have turned 17 and taken the basic traffic course, and the car must have an L-plate and an extra mirror
The pupil must have turned 16 and taken the basic traffic course, and the companion must have held a licence for two years
The pupil must have turned 16 and taken the basic traffic course, but L-plates are only required on practice tracks
ra-010.f: Practice driving can start up to 2 years before the age that gives the right to drive - for class B (18) that means from 16 (Road Traffic Act § 26 second paragraph). The practice driving must not cause danger or unnecessary inconvenience (first paragraph), and the private companion must meet the requirements in the regulations, including age and driving experience. Remember also the mandatory basic traffic course first. The companion must be at least 25 and have held a licence for the class continuously for the last five years. The car must have a visible L at the rear and an extra interior mirror for the companion.

sko-071.s: Which sign has this meaning: "Gives advance warning well before the junction of which destinations each lane leads to - on a portal above the road"
a: Portal orientation board
Portal direction sign
End of temporary diversion
Chains
sko-071.f: Sign 709 "Portal orientation board" (Sign Regulations § 16, the individual direction signs). The sign shows which directions or destinations the lanes are intended for.

sko-073.s: Which sign has this meaning: "Shows the destinations for the lanes on a portal at the junction itself or at the exit"
a: Ordinary direction sign
Table direction sign
Portal orientation board
Portal direction sign
sko-073.f: Sign 719 "Portal direction sign" (Sign Regulations § 16, the individual direction signs). The sign shows which destinations the lanes are intended for.

sku-019.s: The traffic light shows a green arrow. What does the signal mean?
a: A green arrow means you may drive in any direction from the lane
A green arrow applies only to driving in the arrow's direction
A green arrow applies only to cyclists in their own lane
A green arrow means you have priority over oncoming traffic in every direction
sku-019.f: Sign/marking 1082 "Arrow signal" (Sign Regulations § 24, the individual signals). The signal applies to those who want to drive in the direction the arrow shows. An arrow signal can have one, two or three light openings.

fa-005.s: In which of these situations must you take particular care to keep your speed low and, if necessary, stop immediately?
a: Where children are on or beside the road
Where adults are waiting for a green light at a pedestrian crossing
At a green light in a signalled junction with many waiting cars
Where cyclists are riding in a cycle lane on your side
fa-005.f: The Traffic Rules § 13 no. 2 gives an exhaustive list of those for whom you must take particular care to keep your speed low and, if necessary, stop immediately: children who are on or beside the road, school patrols, a person using a white cane or a guide dog, another person who may be assumed to have an impairment or illness that hinders them in traffic, and a tram or bus that has stopped or is about to stop at a stop. A common misunderstanding: that pedestrian crossings belong on this list. Pedestrian crossings are governed by § 9 no. 2, and where traffic is controlled by traffic light signals it is the signal that applies - then it is not § 13 no. 2 that decides.

fd-001.s: How long is a class B driving licence valid, and when is a medical certificate required in order to keep your driving entitlement?
a: 15 years at a time - a medical certificate is required from the age of 80
15 years at a time - a medical certificate is required from the age of 75
10 years at a time - a medical certificate is required from the age of 70
5 years at a time - an eyesight test is required at every renewal
fd-001.f: A driving licence in class B is issued with 15 years of validity (the Driving Licence Regulations § 4-1 first paragraph). It is the card itself that expires, not the driving entitlement: you order a new card with a new photograph, without a new theory test or practical test. To maintain the driving entitlement from the age of 80 there is a requirement of renewal with a medical certificate, and the certificate may be issued with up to three years of validity. A common misunderstanding: that the limit is 75 - it is 80. The heavy classes (C and D with their subgroups) are another matter: they are given five years of validity and require a medical certificate at every renewal.

gs-010.s: What applies to you as a motorist where there is a cycle lane?
a: You must keep out of the lane, and give way when you cross it
You may drive in the lane when there are no cyclists in it
You may stop briefly in the lane when you have a clear view behind
You may use the lane when you are turning right at the junction
gs-010.f: A cycle lane (sykkelfelt) is a traffic lane which by official traffic sign and road marking is designated for cyclists (the Traffic Rules § 1). Drivers other than cyclists must not use it (§ 4 no. 1 first paragraph), and stopping in a cycle lane is prohibited (§ 17 no. 1). If you are going to turn and cross the lane, you must give way to cyclists going straight ahead (§ 7 no. 3). A common misunderstanding: that the car should move into the cycle lane before turning right, as is done in some other countries. In Norway you stay in the traffic lane and cross only when the cycle lane is clear.

ly-015.s: You are approaching the junction just as the traffic light changes from green to amber. What applies?
a: Amber means stop - you drive on only if you cannot stop without danger
Amber means clear to go - speed up so that you get across before it turns red
Amber has the same meaning as red - a full stop no matter where you are
Amber means stop only if pedestrians are standing waiting at the junction
ly-015.f: Amber light on its own warns that the change to red will follow immediately, and that drivers must stop (the Sign Regulations § 24, signal 1080 Main signal). You may nevertheless pass the signal or the stop line if the vehicle has come so far forward that stopping cannot be done without danger. The other way round, red and amber together mean that green is coming immediately - but you must wait until it actually is green. A common misunderstanding: that amber is a signal to hurry across. Amber is a stop signal, and the exception applies only where stopping would be dangerous.

mt-004.s: Traffic is at a standstill in two lanes on the motorway. How do you form an emergency corridor (redningsgate) for emergency vehicles?
a: The left lane moves towards the left, the right lane towards the right
The left lane moves towards the right, the right lane towards the left
All lanes move towards the right, so that the left side is clear
Everyone pulls out onto the hard shoulder, so that the middle of the road is clear
mt-004.f: The emergency corridor is formed between the lanes: if you are in the left lane you move towards the left, and if you are in any other lane you move towards the right. That opens a free corridor in the middle of the road for the emergency vehicle to come through. The corridor itself has no separate provision in the Traffic Rules - the duty follows from § 10 no. 1, where a road user must give free passage to an emergency vehicle and stop if necessary, and from the basic rule in the Road Traffic Act § 3. A common misunderstanding: that you can wait until the blue light is behind you. By then the queue is too dense for anyone to move, so the corridor is formed as soon as traffic comes to a stop.

nt-015.s: You are driving a car with a trailer on a motorway with a speed limit of 110 km/h. What is the highest legal speed for you?
a: 80 km/h
90 km/h
110 km/h
70 km/h
nt-015.f: On a road section with a special speed limit higher than 80 km/h, a motor vehicle with a permissible gross weight over 3500 kg, and every motor vehicle with a trailer, must not be driven faster than 80 km/h (the Traffic Rules § 13 no. 4). The posted 110 therefore does not apply to you when you have a trailer. Two exceptions are worth knowing: a vehicle combination where both the car and the trailer meet the requirements of the Vehicle Use Regulations § 4-4 and § 4-5 may be driven at up to 100 km/h, and a motor vehicle in group M1 without a trailer with a permissible gross weight not over 7500 kg (typically a motorhome) is not covered by the 80 cap. A common misunderstanding: that the 80 cap applies only to heavy vehicles - it is triggered just as much by a small trailer behind an ordinary car.

ra-013.s: The police stop you in a routine check and want to take a breath test. Can you refuse to blow?
a: No - a breath test may be taken without suspicion, and refusing leads to a blood test
Yes - a breath test at a check requires concrete suspicion of impairment
Yes - you may demand a blood test at a doctor instead of blowing
No - but refusing has no consequences if you turn out to be sober
ra-013.f: The police may take a breath test (preliminary breath sample) from the driver of a motor vehicle at a check without any requirement of suspicion (the Road Traffic Act § 22a). Refusing without valid grounds gives authority to bring you in for a blood test - evasion does not help you.

si-021.s: On a narrow country road you catch up with a rider on horseback. How do you pass?
a: At low speed and with a good lateral distance, ready to stop
At normal speed and lateral distance, as when passing another car
Close and fast, so that you are past before the horse has time to react
With a short toot of the horn first, so that the rider knows you are coming
si-021.f: The Traffic Rules apply so far as they are suitable also to a rider and to the person handling a riding animal (§ 2 no. 2), but no separate provision regulates how you pass a horse. The requirement follows from the basic rule in the Road Traffic Act § 3 on conducting yourself considerately and attentively. A horse can be frightened by noise and rapid movements and react unpredictably, so you reduce speed, give a good lateral distance, avoid abrupt manoeuvres and are ready to stop. A common misunderstanding: that a short toot warns the rider in a friendly way. A sound signal is precisely what frightens the horse, and unnecessary use of it is prohibited as well (the Traffic Rules § 14 no. 1).

a: Danger: loose chippings - stones from the car ahead may hit the windscreen
Danger: landslide - stone, earth or snow may be lying on the carriageway
Danger: dangerous verge - the road edge is weak and may give way
Danger: roadworks - construction machinery and loose gravel on the carriageway
sk-009.f: Sign 114 «Rasfare» (danger of landslide) (the Sign Regulations § 4). The sign warns of the danger of a fall of stone, earth, snow or the like, and that fallen material may be lying on the carriageway. The most common confusion is with sign 112 «Steinsprut» (loose chippings): there the stone comes from the wheels of other vehicles on the road, while a landslide comes from above, from the mountainside or the slope beside the road. If you see this sign: reduce speed and look out for loose stone on the road surface, especially after rain, frost and thaw.

a: Prohibited for vehicles with a gross weight higher than indicated
Prohibited for vehicles with an axle load higher than indicated
Prohibited for vehicles with a bogie load higher than indicated
Prohibited for vehicles that have more than two axles
sk-052.f: Sign 322 «Boggilastgrense» (bogie load limit) (the Sign Regulations § 8). The prohibition applies to vehicles with an actual bogie load higher than indicated. Bogie load is the combined weight on two axles placed close together - a bogie. By comparison, sign 320 «Aksellastgrense» (axle load limit) applies to the weight on one axle, and sign 318 «Totalvektgrense» (gross weight limit) to the weight of the whole vehicle. The symbol decides which of them you have in front of you: 322 shows the figure above two wheels, 320 above one wheel, and 318 has only the figure inside the red ring.

sko-033.s: Which sign has this meaning: «No one may overtake a motor vehicle with more than two wheels on this section»
a: No overtaking
No overtaking for lorries
End of no overtaking
End of no overtaking for lorries
sko-033.f: Sign 334 «Forbikjøringsforbud» (no overtaking) (the Sign Regulations § 8). The prohibition applies to overtaking a motor vehicle that has more than two wheels, so you may still overtake a motorcycle, a moped and a bicycle. Nor does the prohibition apply to overtaking which under the Traffic Rules may lawfully take place on the right. It lasts until sign 336 «Slutt på forbikjøringsforbud» (end of no overtaking), or over the section indicated on a supplementary plate. Sign 335 is the narrower variant: there it is only lorries with a permissible gross weight over 3500 kg that may not overtake.

sko-097.s: Which marker has this meaning: «Keep within the lane you have been guided into»
a: Tunnel marker
Obstruction marker
Traffic cylinder
Edge post
sko-097.f: Sign 942 «Trafikksylinder» (traffic cylinder) (the Sign Regulations § 20). The cylinder indicates either that road users are to keep within the lane they have been guided into, or other conditions road users must be aware of. It is used in particular at roadworks and where traffic is temporarily rerouted. Note that 940 «Trafikkjegle» (traffic cone) has word for word the same meaning in the regulations - the difference is only the shape, cylinder against cone. The two others in this question do something else: the edge post (920) marks where the edge of the road runs, and the obstruction marker (908) marks an obstruction on or near the carriageway.

sp-009.s: Your engine breaks down on the motorway and you get the car out onto the hard shoulder. What do you do first?
a: Switch on the hazard lights, put on a reflective vest and go behind the crash barrier
Stay seated in the car with your seat belt on until help arrives
Put out the warning triangle right behind the car and wait there
Position yourself in front of the car so that traffic behind sees you early
sp-009.f: Stopping is prohibited on a motorway and on a motor traffic road (the Traffic Rules § 17 no. 1), so an emergency stop must be handled as a dangerous situation. The order is: right out onto the hard shoulder or into a lay-by, hazard lights on, reflective vests on everyone who is getting out, out of the car on the side facing away from the traffic, and then behind the crash barrier - after that you call for help. A reflective vest must be used when a person moves outside the vehicle during an emergency stop along a road, and the warning triangle is put out a good distance behind the car, if possible at least 150 metres, but only if it can be done safely (the Vehicle Use Regulations § 1-6). A common misunderstanding: staying seated in the car with the seat belt on. With traffic passing at 110 km/h, a stationary car beside the carriageway is exactly where you should not be.

vp-013.s: Part of the road is blocked by a parked vehicle on your side. A car is coming towards you. Who must wait?
a: You - the one who has the obstruction on their side must give way
The oncoming driver - the one who has the obstruction on their side has priority
Whoever reaches the obstruction last must wait
Neither has a duty to give way - you sort it out with signals and lights
vp-013.f: If part of the road is blocked, the one who has the obstruction on their side must give way (the Traffic Rules § 7 no. 6). So you must wait behind the obstruction until oncoming traffic has passed.

fa-019.s: A motor vehicle with a permissible gross weight over 3 500 kg is driving on a road posted 100 km/h. What is the vehicle's maximum speed?
a: 80 km/h
100 km/h
90 km/h
70 km/h
fa-019.f: On a road section with a speed limit higher than 80 km/h, a motor vehicle with a permissible gross weight over 3 500 kg - and any motor vehicle with a trailer - must not be driven faster than 80 km/h (the Traffic Rules § 13 no. 4). The same provision lists the exceptions: emergency vehicles, a motor vehicle in group M1 (car, motorhome) without a trailer with a permissible gross weight up to 7 500 kg and tyres rated for the speed limit at the place, a bus without a trailer registered in class III or bus class 3 (up to 100 km/h), and a car with a trailer where both meet the requirements of the Vehicle Use Regulations § 4-4 and § 4-5, that is Tempo 100 (up to 100 km/h). With class B you do not drive anything heavier than 3 500 kg, so the main rule of 80 km/h is the one you need to know. A common misunderstanding: that the posted figure applies to everyone - a speed limit sign is a ceiling, not a permission.

gs-004.s: On a country road with no pavement and no usable shoulder, pedestrians have to walk in the carriageway. Which side must they use?
a: Farthest to the left in the direction of walking - but farthest to the right if they are wheeling a bicycle
Farthest to the right in the direction of walking - the same side as the traffic drives
Farthest to the right in the direction of walking - but farthest to the left if they are wheeling a bicycle
Farthest to the left in the direction of walking - also when wheeling a bicycle
gs-004.f: The Traffic Rules § 19 no. 1 sets the order of priority: pedestrians must use a footpath, a pavement or the shoulder of the road, and may walk in a cycle path, a cycle lane or the carriageway only when that is not possible or reasonable. Once you are in the carriageway, you must walk farthest to the left in the direction of walking - but farthest to the right if you are wheeling a bicycle (the law says «leier sykkel», which means the same). The left side gives you eye contact with oncoming traffic, so you see the car and the car sees you. If you are wheeling a bicycle you walk on the right, so that the bicycle is not left sticking out into the carriageway towards oncoming cars. The opposite side may be used if you would otherwise be exposed to danger, for example in a blind left-hand bend.

kj-013.s: What is the correct seating position behind the wheel?
a: A straight arm reaching the top of the wheel, and the head restraint level with the top of your head
A straight arm reaching the top of the wheel, and the head restraint level with your neck
As close to the wheel as possible - a short distance gives the fastest and safest steering
The seat as low as possible - that gives a low centre of gravity and the best control
kj-013.f: A correct seating position gives you control and lets the seat belt and the airbag work as they were designed to. You test the distance with a straight arm: your wrist should reach the top of the steering wheel while you are sitting well back in the seat. If you sit too close, the injury risk from the airbag increases; if you sit too far away, you lose steering and braking force. The head restraint must catch your head in a rear-end collision, and for that its top edge must at least reach the top of your head, with the restraint close to the back of your head. A common misunderstanding: that the head restraint is a neck rest and should be at neck height - set that low, it works as a pivot point and can make whiplash injury worse instead of preventing it. The requirements for preparing the car for driving are part of stage 2 of the curriculum for class B (the Norwegian Public Roads Administration, HB V851).

mo-006.s: What do the Traffic Rules require of the way you drive in or near built-up areas?
a: Your route, speed and manner of driving must be adapted so that no one is unnecessarily disturbed
Speed and manner of driving must be adapted - which route you choose is your own decision
The manner of driving must be adapted - speed is covered anyway by the local speed limit
The requirement applies only at night, between 23:00 and 06:00
mo-006.f: The Traffic Rules § 16 no. 2: in or near built-up areas, the route, speed and manner of driving must be adapted so that no one is unnecessarily disturbed. The route is thus part of the requirement - if you drive round and round through a residential street, it is the route itself that is the problem, even if you keep to the speed limit. § 16 no. 1 covers the other side: there, unnecessary and disturbing driving with a motor vehicle is prohibited, as is idling and other use of a motor vehicle that causes unnecessary noise or unnecessary emission of smoke or gas. It is no. 1 that catches revving the engine and the sound system at full volume. A common misunderstanding: that this applies only at night - the provisions apply around the clock, and the local speed limit is a ceiling, not a guarantee that your speed is adapted.

mt-008.s: Why must the gap to the car ahead be much longer at 110 km/h than at 50 km/h?
a: Because you travel much further in three seconds - over 90 metres
Because your reaction time gets longer the faster you drive
Because the Traffic Rules require at least a 100 metre gap on a motorway
Because braking distance only doubles when you double the speed
mt-008.f: The distance requirement in the Traffic Rules § 5 no. 3 is not given in figures: the distance to the vehicle ahead must be large enough that no danger of collision arises if the vehicle ahead slows down or stops. That is why the gap is measured in time, not in metres. Three seconds is around 42 metres at 50 km/h and over 90 metres at 110 km/h (110 km/h is 30.5 metres per second). Your reaction time is the same whatever the speed - it is the distance you cover while reacting that grows, and braking distance quadruples when speed doubles. Add § 13 no. 1: you must be able to stop within the stretch of road you can see. A common misunderstanding: that there is a limit in metres to look up - there is none, and the most common motorway accidents are precisely rear-end collisions caused by following too closely.

pf-020.s: You are going to turn right at a junction, but you are positioned well in towards the middle of the carriageway. What is the problem?
a: Others read you wrongly, and a cyclist may come up on your inside
Nothing, as long as you signal right in good time
Nothing in a junction with no traffic - positioning is a formality
Only that the turn becomes technically harder for you yourself
pf-020.f: The positioning rules in the Traffic Rules § 6 make you predictable: others read what you are going to do from where you are positioned, before you indicate. Positioning close to the right before a right turn closes the gap a cyclist could otherwise have used on the inside - one of the most common serious cycling accidents.

si-011.s: You are driving car A out of a petrol station and are going to turn left onto the road. Car B is coming from the left and car C from the right. Who must give way?
a: Only car C concerns me - the right-hand rule applies as usual
Car B and car C must both let me out onto the road
I must give way to both car B and car C
Whoever reaches the exit first goes first
si-011.f: A driver coming from a car park, a stopping place, a square, a property, a petrol station, a pedestrian street or a home zone must give way to other road users (the Traffic Rules § 7 no. 4). The duty to give way applies to traffic in both directions, so you must wait for both car B from the left and car C from the right - and you must not merely let them pass, you must also avoid forcing them to brake or swerve. A common misunderstanding: that the right-hand rule applies here, so that only the car from the right concerns you. The right-hand rule applies between roads that meet at a junction, not when you drive out onto the road from an area beside it.

si-023.s: Your trailer is Tempo 100 approved, and the car and the trailer meet the requirements. What is the highest permitted speed on a motorway with a speed limit of 110?
a: 80 km/h - the limit for driving with a trailer applies regardless
100 km/h - the approval raises the limit from 80 to 100
110 km/h - I may follow the posted speed limit
90 km/h - Tempo 100 applies only abroad
si-023.f: With a trailer the limit is 80 km/h on a road with a speed limit higher than 80 (the Traffic Rules § 13 no. 4). The same provision makes an exception for a motor vehicle and a trailer that both meet the requirements of the Regulations on the use of vehicles § 4-4 and § 4-5, that is Tempo 100. Such a combination may be driven at up to 100 km/h, but never faster than the posted speed limit. A common misunderstanding: that the approval lets you follow the posted 110 - the ceiling is 100 km/h however high the posted limit is, and both parts of the combination must be approved, not only the trailer.

a: Stop only if there is crossing traffic
Come to a full stop, and give way to drivers on the crossing road
Give way to drivers on the crossing road, but without a duty to stop
Stopping is compulsory only for a check by police or customs
sk-037.f: Sign 204 «Stopp» (stop) (the Sign Regulations § 6). Drivers must come to a full stop before driving onto the crossing road or before crossing a level crossing, and must give way to traffic in both directions on the crossing road, or give free passage to a tram or a train at the level crossing. The stop must be made in front of and up against the stop line, and where there is no stop line, as close to the crossing road as possible. A common misunderstanding: that it is enough to roll slowly forward when you can see that it is clear - the duty to stop applies regardless, and it is precisely that duty which distinguishes sign 204 from sign 202 «Vikeplikt» (give way), where you only have a duty to give way.

a: It is prohibited to overtake a motor vehicle with more than two wheels
It is prohibited for lorries over 3 500 kg to overtake other vehicles
It is prohibited to overtake any vehicle, including bicycles and mopeds
Give way to oncoming traffic where the road is narrow
sk-057.f: Sign 334 «Forbikjøringsforbud» (no overtaking) (the Sign Regulations § 8). The prohibition applies to overtaking a motor vehicle that has more than two wheels - so you may still overtake a bicycle, a moped and a two-wheeled motorcycle, as long as it is done safely. Nor does the prohibition apply to overtaking which under the Traffic Rules may lawfully take place on the right, and it lasts until sign 336 «Slutt på forbikjøringsforbud» (end of no overtaking) or as far as a supplementary plate indicates. A common misunderstanding: reading the sign as a prohibition aimed at a particular group of vehicles. That is sign 335, which prohibits lorries over 3 500 kg from overtaking. On 334 the sign says what you may not overtake, not who the prohibition applies to.

sko-046.s: Which sign has this meaning: «From here the same traffic rules apply as on a motorway, but the road lacks a central barrier or grade-separated junctions»
a: Motorway
Motor traffic road
End of motorway
Heavy vehicle lane
sko-046.f: Sign 503 «Motortrafikkveg» (motor traffic road) (the Sign Regulations § 12). The sign indicates that the provisions of the Traffic Rules on motor traffic roads apply from the sign until sign 505 «Slutt på motortrafikkveg» (end of motor traffic road), until sign 502 «Motorveg» (motorway), or until a junction with a road that is not a motor traffic road. The rules are the same as on a motorway: only a motor vehicle or a vehicle combination that may lawfully be driven at at least 40 km/h, and mopeds are excluded (the Traffic Rules § 4 no. 2), stopping is prohibited (§ 17 no. 1), and reversing and turning round are prohibited (§ 11 no. 2). The difference between the two lies in the standard, not in the rules: a motorway always has a central barrier and grade-separated junctions, while a motor traffic road lacks at least one of these. The speed limit is posted separately on both.

sku-006.s: You are driving on a road with combined lines. The line nearest you is broken. What applies?
a: You may cross when conditions allow - the line nearest you applies
You may not cross - when one of the lines is solid, it applies both ways
You may cross, but only in order to turn off to the left
You must wait until both lines are broken
sku-006.f: Road marking 1006 «Kombinerte linjer» (combined lines) (the Sign Regulations § 22): where there are combined lines, drivers must follow the line that is nearest. If the line nearest you is broken, you may cross - but only when visibility and traffic allow it, because the overtaking rules in the Traffic Rules § 12 apply just as much, and a broken line is a permission, not an invitation. Anyone who has moved over into the lane for oncoming traffic may always return to the right-hand side of the road, even across a solid line. A common misunderstanding: that the solid line applies both ways - then the whole point of combined lines would fall away, because they are used precisely where one direction has enough visibility for overtaking and the other does not.

vl-009.s: Which light does this warning lamp show?
a: The main beam
The dipped beam
The front fog lights
The daytime running lights
vl-009.f: The symbol is the main beam: a lamp with straight, horizontal rays (ISO 7000-0082). On the instrument panel this lamp shows blue, and blue is reserved for the main beam. The dipped beam has the same lamp, but the rays slope downwards, and the lamp is green (ISO 7000-0083). Front fog lights are recognised by the wavy line running across the rays. The blue lamp is the reminder to dip: the main beam must not be used in such a way that another road user is dazzled, and the same applies when meeting a train, a tram or a vessel travelling along the road (the Traffic Rules § 15 no. 2). A common misunderstanding: mixing up main beam and dipped beam because the lamp is the same - it is the direction of the rays that separates them.

vp-023.s: You are driving on a narrow road and meet this sign. What does it mean for you?
a: You must give way to oncoming drivers in the narrow stretch
Oncoming drivers must give way to you in the narrow stretch
The road is one-way through the narrow stretch
Nobody has a duty to give way - the sign only warns that the road is narrow
vp-023.f: Sign 212 «Vikeplikt overfor møtende kjørende» (give way to oncoming traffic) (the Sign Regulations § 6). The sign prohibits you from driving onto the narrow stretch of road if doing so would obstruct oncoming drivers - so you must wait until the road is clear. If nothing is coming towards you, you drive on. On the other side of the narrow stretch stands sign 214 «Møtende kjørende har vikeplikt» (oncoming traffic must give way), a blue square sign telling the others that they may go first. A common misunderstanding: mixing up the two signs. Remember the colours and the arrows - the red, round sign means you wait, the blue, square one means the others wait. Drive carefully all the same: the sign is no guarantee that everyone observes the duty, and on a narrow road you rarely have room to correct a misunderstanding.

fb-008.s: When should you move back in to the right after an overtaking?
a: When you can move in without obstructing or endangering the vehicle you have overtaken
Immediately when your front end is past - a quick move in gives the least time in the oncoming lane
As soon as you see the overtaken vehicle in your door mirror - then you are clear of it
When the overtaken driver flashes their lights to show that you may move in
fb-008.f: A driver who has overtaken on the left must move back to the right when the overtaking is completed, without causing danger to, obstructing or unnecessarily disturbing the vehicle overtaken (the Traffic Rules § 12 no. 3). A practical rule of thumb: wait until you can see the whole car in the interior mirror. If you can see it only in the door mirror, you are still too close. The rule of thumb is an aid to fulfilling the requirement, it is not a legal rule of its own, and neither a flash of the lights from the overtaken driver nor the fact that your front end is past gives you the go-ahead.

gs-006.s: Which rules apply to electric scooters (small electric motor vehicles)?
a: They mainly follow the cycling rules - cycle paths and cycle lanes are allowed
They follow the moped rules - the carriageway is the only lawful place
They follow the rules for pedestrians - the pavement is the only lawful place
They follow the cycling rules - but are permitted only from the age of 18
gs-006.f: A small electric motor vehicle (electric scooter) mainly follows the cycling rules: it may use cycle paths and cycle lanes, but only on the right-hand side of the road (the Traffic Rules § 4 no. 1), and it may be ridden on the right-hand shoulder of the road (§ 5 no. 1). Pavements and footpaths are not prohibited, but are permitted only where pedestrian traffic is light, and pedestrians must be passed at a good distance and at no more than 6 km/h (§ 20 no. 3). The age limit is 12 (the Driving Licence Regulations), not 18. For you as a motorist: treat the electric scooter as a cyclist when you are turning - you must give way to anyone going straight ahead (§ 7 no. 3).

kj-018.s: You are driving in winter conditions and feel the stability control (ESC/ESP) intervene. What does that tell you?
a: That you were at the limit of the available grip - the speed must come down
That the ESC has switched off the ABS brakes until the situation is over
That the car has full control - you can keep the same speed
That the tyres are new and have not yet developed full grip
kj-018.f: ESC brakes individual wheels to counteract a skid when the car is about to lose grip. A flashing ESC lamp is a warning that you are driving too fast for the conditions. The system does not extend the limits of physics, it only makes use of the grip that is there, and it does not switch off the ABS - the two systems work together. Adapting your speed is your own responsibility (the Road Traffic Act § 6).

mr-007.s: What should you do when you notice drowsiness behind the wheel on a long drive?
a: Stop in a safe place and take a short nap of about a quarter of an hour
Turn up the music and open the window - that will last the rest of the trip
Drink coffee and drive on straight away - the caffeine works immediately
Carry on - the drowsiness passes by itself once you get moving
mr-007.f: Driving a vehicle when you are «tired or fatigued» is prohibited under the Road Traffic Act § 21. The only thing that really removes drowsiness is sleep: stop in a safe place and take a short nap. You may well drink coffee just before the nap, because the caffeine only takes effect after 20-30 minutes - that is why the two work well together, while coffee and driving on straight away does not. Fresh air and music give only a few minutes of relief, and microsleep comes without warning. Plan breaks roughly every two hours, and remember that night and early morning are the body's low points.

mt-009.s: You pass this sign. What does it mean for the rules from here on?
a: A prohibition on stopping, reversing and turning round - and only motor vehicles capable of 40 km/h
A prohibition on stopping and turning round - but reversing on the shoulder is allowed if you take a wrong turn
The speed limit becomes 110 km/h, and all motor vehicles may use the road regardless
The rules apply only until the first exit - there the sign must be repeated
mt-009.f: Sign 502 «Motorveg» (motorway) indicates that the provisions of the Traffic Rules on motorways apply from the sign until sign 504 «Slutt på motorveg» (end of motorway), until sign 503 «Motortrafikkveg» (motor traffic road), or until the junction between the exit road and a road that is not a motorway (the Sign Regulations § 12). Three things then apply: only a motor vehicle or a vehicle combination that may lawfully be driven at at least 40 km/h may drive there (the Traffic Rules § 4 no. 2), reversing and turning round are prohibited (§ 11 no. 2), and stopping is prohibited (§ 17 no. 1). The speed limit does not follow from this sign; it is posted separately.

ra-002.s: You are driving the day after a party and feel in fine shape. A check shows 0.3 per mille of alcohol in your blood. What happens?
a: You will be punished - believing you were sober is no defence
You escape punishment because you were in good faith about your own condition
You escape punishment because the limit is 0.5 per mille
You get only a warning the first time it happens
ra-002.f: The alcohol limit in Norway is 0.2 per mille (the Road Traffic Act § 22 second paragraph), and «a mistake as to the size of the alcohol concentration does not exempt from punishment» (§ 22 fourth paragraph). It is your responsibility to be certain that you are sober enough. At 0.3 per mille the reaction is normally a fine (§ 31 second paragraph), not a warning. A classic trap: alcohol is broken down more slowly than people think, so «the day after» you may still be over the limit even though you feel in fine shape.

si-019.s: You are driving car A and are about to reverse out of a parking bay. Car B is coming along the street. What do you do?
a: Wait until car B has passed - the one reversing gives way to all traffic
Reverse out at once, so that I get out before car B arrives
Reverse out - car B must give way because I am coming from the right
Whichever of us has the better view should give way
si-019.f: A driver who reverses or turns round must give way to other road users (the Traffic Rules § 11 no. 1) - no matter who arrived first, and no matter who is coming from the right. If the view is not sufficient, you must either have someone else keeping watch, or have got out yourself and made sure that it is clear. The right-hand rule in § 7 no. 2 applies at road junctions, not when you are reversing out of a parking bay.

si-024.s: On a multi-lane road you are in the lane to the right of a lorry, roughly level with the cab. Why should you not stay there?
a: You are in the lorry's largest blind spot and will probably not be seen
The lorry has a longer braking distance and may run into you from behind
The air pressure from the lorry can push your car off the road
It is prohibited to travel alongside a lorry on a multi-lane road
si-024.f: The area immediately to the right of the cab is the lorry's largest blind spot. If you cannot see the driver in his mirror, he cannot see you. Stay either well ahead or well behind, never alongside for any length of time. There is no separate prohibition on being there; it is the duty of care in the Road Traffic Act § 3 that makes it irresponsible.

a: A dangerous junction where the right-hand rule applies
Crossing traffic must give way to you until it is cancelled
Warning of one junction where traffic from the side road must give way
You must give way to all traffic from the crossing road
sk-040.f: Sign 210 «Forkjørskryss» (priority junction) (the Sign Regulations § 6). The sign warns of one dangerous road junction where drivers from the side road or the crossing road have been given a duty to give way by sign 202 «Vikeplikt» (give way) or 204 «Stopp» (stop). The most common confusion: 206 «Forkjørsveg» (priority road) is not a warning of a single junction, but a status that applies until it is cancelled by sign 208, 202 or 204. And 124 «Farlig vegkryss» (dangerous junction) looks almost the same - red triangle against red triangle - but there the ordinary duty to give way to traffic from the right applies. The thick vertical bar is the difference.

a: It shows the direction in which the road curves
It marks a sharp bend - placed on the outside of the curve
The diagonal stripes point down towards the side you may pass on
The diagonal stripes point down towards the side you may not pass on
sk-180.f: Sign 906 «Hindermarkering» (obstruction marker) (the Sign Regulations § 20). The regulations put it like this: «The diagonal stripes point down towards the side on which the marker may be passed.» The stripes therefore slope towards the side you are to drive on, not away from it. Do not confuse the sign with 904 «Retningsmarkering» (direction marker), which is set up on the outside of a curve and shows which way the road turns.

sko-089.s: Which supplementary plate (shown beneath a main sign) has this meaning: «An arrow showing in which direction along the road the main sign's rule on stopping or parking applies»
a: Advance warning of stop
Extent of stopping and parking regulation
Extent
Combined regulation
sko-089.f: Sign 828 «Utstrekning av stans- og parkeringsregulering» (extent of stopping and parking regulation) (the Sign Regulations § 18). The supplementary plate indicates that the regulation applies in the direction of the arrow, possibly over the distance stated: 828.1 applies in both directions of travel, 828.2 applies against the direction of travel, 828.3 applies in the direction of travel. The plate may also be mounted horizontally, and the arrow symbols may be used on other supplementary plates that regulate stopping or parking. Do not confuse it with 804 «Utstrekning» (extent), which with figures in metres states the distance to the beginning and the end of the road section.

sp-005.s: You stop 10 metres from the sign for a bus stop in order to let a passenger out. Is that allowed?
a: Yes - setting down and picking up is allowed when you do not obstruct the bus
Yes - the 20 metre rule applies only to parking, not to stopping
No - all stopping is prohibited closer than 20 metres from the sign
No - stopping is only allowed inside the bus bay itself
sp-005.f: It is prohibited to stop on a road widening for a stop or closer than 20 metres from an official traffic sign for a bus, taxi or tram stop. Exception: setting down or picking up passengers where this does not obstruct a bus, a taxi or a tram (the Traffic Rules § 17 no. 1). Note that the bus bay itself is the worst place to stop - the prohibition covers both the bay and the 20 metres from the sign.

vp-005.s: You are cycling on a cycle path that runs separately from the road. The cycle path crosses the road, and the crossing is not signposted. What applies?
a: You must give way to the traffic on the road
The traffic on the road must give way to you
The right-hand rule decides - if you come from the right, you go first
You must give way only if the crossing is not road-marked
vp-005.f: A driver who is going to enter or cross a road from a cycle path, a footpath or a pavement must give way to road users on the road (the Traffic Rules § 7 no. 4). That also applies where the crossing is road-marked - the marking alone does not move the duty to give way. If, on the other hand, the car is coming out of a car park, a property or a petrol station, it is the driver of the car who must give way. The right-hand rule does not decide this; § 7 no. 4 takes precedence.

vp-029.s: You are approaching a junction with this sign. The junction is empty and you have a full view. Must you reduce your speed?
a: Yes - your speed must be low enough for you to be able to stop
Yes - the sign requires you always to come to a full stop
No - with a full view you may keep your speed
No - the sign applies only when traffic is coming
vp-029.f: Sign 202 imposes a duty to give way to traffic on the crossing road. If there is no one to give way to, the sign does not require a full stop - that is what sign 204 «Stopp» (stop) does. But the Traffic Rules § 7 no. 1 says that a driver with a duty to give way must show it clearly by reducing speed in good time or by stopping, and your speed must in any case be low enough for you to be able to stop if your assessment of the junction turns out to be wrong.

fa-013.s: You are driving into a residential area and pass this sign. What does it mean?
a: The speed limit applies on all roads in the area until it is revoked
The speed limit applies only on the road where the sign stands
The speed limit applies until the first junction you pass
The speed limit is advisory - it recommends, but does not require
fa-013.f: Sign 366 "Speed limit zone" marks a zone where it is prohibited to drive faster than the number of km/h shown on the sign (the Sign Regulations section 8). The limit applies on all roads inside the zone, not just on the road you entered on, and it lasts until it is revoked by sign 368 "End of speed limit zone", sign 540 "Home zone" or sign 548 "Pedestrian street". The sign also warns that there may be physical speed humps in the carriageway. The difference from the ordinary speed limit sign 362 is the reach: 362 applies along one stretch of road until another speed limit is signposted, while the zone sign covers the whole area you are inside. The speed limit is moreover a ceiling, not a recommendation - if visibility is poor or children are playing outside, you must stay below it anyway.

fd-003.s: What is the probationary period for a driving licence, and what does it involve?
a: 2 years - double penalty points, and loss of the licence means a new driving test
6 months with a ban on night driving and on passengers under 20 years of age
1 year in which all driving must take place with an experienced accompanying driver in the passenger seat
2 years - but the probationary period applies only until you turn 20
fd-003.f: When a category B licence is issued for the first time or extended to, a probationary period of 2 years is set, and it is noted on the licence (the Driving Licence Regulations section 4-2 first paragraph). Two things separate this period from the time afterwards. Every offence gives double penalty points, so the limit of eight points is reached twice as fast - two ordinary fines can be enough. And if you lose your licence during the probationary period as a result of breaching the rules of conduct in traffic, you must sit a new full driving test, that is both the theory test and the practical test; after passing, a new probationary period of 2 years begins, also on later repetitions (section 4-2 second paragraph). The probationary period has nothing to do with age, and it gives no separate rules about night driving, passengers or an accompanying driver.

kj-007.s: What do you look for when you check the steering during the safety check?
a: Play in the steering wheel, unusual noise, or the car pulling to one side
That the power steering works - without power steering the car is illegal to use
That the steering wheel sits straight - a crooked wheel is the only sign of a steering fault
Nothing - the steering is covered by the periodic technical inspection every second year
kj-007.f: Before driving begins, the driver must make sure that the vehicle is in a safe and roadworthy condition, and see to it that it also remains so during use (the Road Traffic Act section 23 first paragraph). Steering and brakes are the two systems that must work for the car to be called safe. On the steering you look for three things: noticeable play, that is that the steering wheel can be moved before the wheels respond; unusual noise or jerking when you turn; and the car pulling to one side when you hold the wheel straight on a level road. The last of these may just as well be caused by low tyre pressure or incorrect wheel alignment, but all three are signs that something must be examined before you drive on. A failure of the power steering makes the wheel heavy, but no rule says that the car is therefore automatically illegal - it is the safe condition that is the requirement. And the periodic technical inspection does not exempt you: the duty under section 23 applies on every single trip.

mk-008.s: You have a breakdown in the dark on a rural road. How do you secure the car and yourself?
a: Parking lights and hazard lights on, high-visibility vest on before you get out, warning triangle at least 150 metres behind, everyone out of the carriageway
Parking lights and hazard lights on, high-visibility vest on before you get out, warning triangle 20 metres behind the car, everyone out of the carriageway
Parking lights and hazard lights on, high-visibility vest on before you get out, warning triangle at least 150 metres behind, everyone stays seated
Dipped headlights and hazard lights on, high-visibility vest on before you get out, warning triangle at least 150 metres behind, everyone out of the carriageway
mk-008.f: Four things must be in place, and each of the wrong options gets one of them wrong. Parking lights must be lit while stopped on a road when the light or visibility conditions make it necessary in order to make the vehicle visible, and dipped or main beam headlights must not be lit during such a stop - they dazzle oncoming traffic and hide how wide the car is (the Traffic Rules section 15 no. 4). The hazard lights warn that the car is standing still. The high-visibility vest must be used when a person moves outside the vehicle during a breakdown along a road, so put it on before you open the door. The warning triangle must be placed at a good distance, if possible at least 150 metres from the car, so that other drivers see it in time (the Vehicle Use Regulations section 1-6). At 80 km/h you cover 150 metres in under seven seconds, and then it is obvious that 20 metres is too short. Finally, everyone must get out of the carriageway, behind the crash barrier or up into the ditch - staying seated in a dark car on a rural road is the most dangerous choice.

mt-006.s: Your car stops in a tunnel, and you cannot reach an emergency lay-by. What do you do?
a: Switch on the hazard lights, stop the engine and raise the alarm from the tunnel's emergency telephone
Switch on the hazard lights and stay seated in the car with your seat belt on until help arrives
Switch on the hazard lights and turn the car around to drive out the same way you came in
Switch on the hazard lights and call from your mobile - the emergency telephone is only for fire
mt-006.f: Stopping is prohibited in a tunnel (the Traffic Rules section 17 no. 1), so a car left standing there is an immediate danger that must be reported at once. Switch on the hazard lights, stop the engine - a running engine can cause a fire and fills the tunnel with exhaust fumes - and use the tunnel's emergency telephone. It alerts the Road Traffic Centre with your exact position and lets them close the tunnel and set a red light at the entrance. A mobile call does not do the same: there may be no coverage, and you have to explain where you are yourself. The emergency telephone is not reserved for fire. Staying seated is the most dangerous option, because the traffic behind has poor visibility in a tunnel and no way around. Turning around and driving against the direction of travel is life-threatening in a twin-bore tunnel. If a fire starts, this applies in addition: leave the car unlocked with the key in it, and walk to the nearest emergency exit - they are marked with the distance in both directions.

pf-009.s: The bus lane is signposted for buses and taxis. Who may use the lane even though the sign does not mention them?
a: Two-wheeled motorcycles, two-wheeled mopeds and bicycles
Passenger cars with two or more people in the car
All motor vehicles when there is a queue in the ordinary lane
Vans and lorries out on business assignments
pf-009.f: Driving in a bus lane is only permitted as stated on the sign. Nevertheless, electric or hydrogen-powered motor vehicles, two-wheeled motorcycles without a sidecar, two-wheeled mopeds, bicycles, small electric motor vehicles and marked emergency vehicles may use such lanes (the Traffic Rules section 5 no. 2). These groups therefore do not need to be named on the sign. Electric cars are on the same list, but in several places they are shut out or tied to a passenger requirement through local decisions and supplementary signs - among others in Oslo, Akershus and Trondheim, in some places only on weekdays. So always read the supplementary sign. The number of people in the car gives no right to the bus lane; that rule belongs to the carpool lane (sign 509), where the requirement is shown as a number on the sign. A queue in the ordinary lane gives no right either - that is precisely when the lane is meant to let public transport through.

ra-014.s: Why is it dangerous to rely on your own judgement of whether you are sober enough to drive?
a: Alcohol impairs both your driving ability and the judgement that should have stopped you
Alcohol impairs your driving ability, but your judgement stays intact
Alcohol mainly impairs your vision - your reactions hold up longer
Alcohol only impairs fine motor skills, and you notice that clearly yourself
ra-014.f: Alcohol hits two things at the same time. It impairs reaction time, coordination, peripheral vision and the ability to divide your attention between several things - and it impairs the judgement that should have told you not to drive. That is why many people feel sharp while they are in fact impaired, and "I feel fine" is no measure: the person who is under the influence is the least fit to judge their own level of impairment. Nor does the law leave the assessment to the driver. No one may drive a vehicle in a condition where they cannot be regarded as fit to drive safely (the Road Traffic Act section 21), and if you have more than 0.2 per mille of alcohol in your blood, you are in all cases regarded as under the influence (section 22). Being mistaken about your own blood alcohol level does not exempt you from punishment. The only safe rule is to leave the car.

si-022.s: You drive into an environmental street (miljogate). What does that mean for your driving?
a: The street has been rebuilt with narrowings and humps, so the speed must come down
The street is closed to everything except public transport and electric cars
The street is a pedestrian street where only goods deliveries and cycling are permitted
The street has a speed limit of 20 km/h around the clock, even without signs
si-022.f: An environmental street (miljogate) is a through street that has been rebuilt to reduce speed and give more room to pedestrians and cyclists: narrowings, raised pedestrian crossings, humps, side parking and planting. Driving is still permitted for everyone, but the layout demands low speed and extra attention, and you must expect pedestrians crossing between parked cars. "Miljogate" is not a separate rule in the Traffic Rules or the Sign Regulations - it is a way of building the street. It is therefore the signposting that decides the speed, typically 30 or 40 km/h, and if there are no signs, the ordinary limit for built-up areas applies. A pedestrian street and a home zone are something else: they have their own signs (548 and 540) and their own rules on driving and speed.

a: Danger: several dangerous bends
Danger: a single dangerous bend
Danger: steep hill
Danger: road narrows
sk-001.f: Sign 100 "Dangerous bend" (the Sign Regulations section 4). The sign warns of one bend that is sharper than the rest of the stretch, and the arrow shows which way the bend goes. If several bends follow one after another, sign 102 "Dangerous bends" is used - that is the most common mix-up.

a: Come to a complete stop, and give way to drivers on the crossing road
Crossing traffic must give way to you until it is revoked
Give way to drivers in both directions on the crossing road
Give way only to drivers coming from the right
sk-036.f: The sign is 202 "Give way". It states that drivers must give way to driving traffic in both directions on the crossing road (the Sign Regulations section 6). Giving way means that you must not obstruct or disturb the driver who has right of way: if it is clear, you may drive on without stopping, but your speed must be low enough that you can stop if someone comes. Sign 204 "Stop" looks different - an octagon, not a triangle - and additionally requires you to come to a complete stop before you enter the crossing road, in front of the stop line or as close to the crossing road as possible. Sign 206 "Priority road" is the opposite: then it is the others who must give way to you. And the right-hand rule does not apply here; it applies only at junctions without signposting.

a: Stopping prohibited up to the nearest junction
You must stop for customs clearance before driving on
You must stop for an inspection before driving on
Full stop and give way to all crossing traffic
sk-053.f: The sign is 324 "Stop for stated purpose". It prohibits you from driving on until you have stopped for the purpose stated in text on the sign (the Sign Regulations section 8) - here it says "Inspection". The text itself therefore decides what you must stop for, and that is why the sign must be read, not just recognised by its shape. For customs there is a separate sign: 326 "Stop for customs" states a duty to stop for customs clearance. Sign 324 must also not be confused with 204 "Stop", which concerns the duty to stop and give way at a junction, or with 370 "No stopping", which is about where you may not stop.

sko-034.s: Which sign has this meaning: "A lorry with a permitted maximum laden weight over 3 500 kg may not overtake a motor vehicle with more than two wheels"
a: No overtaking
No overtaking by lorries
End of no overtaking by lorries
Maximum laden weight limit
sko-034.f: Sign 335 "No overtaking by lorries" (the Sign Regulations section 8). The prohibition applies to lorries with a permitted maximum laden weight over 3 500 kg overtaking a motor vehicle with more than two wheels. The lorry may therefore still pass motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles, and overtaking that may lawfully be done on the right under the Traffic Rules is not covered. The prohibition lasts until sign 337 "End of no overtaking by lorries", or over the stretch stated on a supplementary sign. Sign 334 "No overtaking" is the broad version: there the prohibition applies to all drivers, not just lorries. Note what the weight tells you: 3 500 kg says who the prohibition applies to, not how heavy the vehicle is allowed to be. The latter is sign 318 "Maximum laden weight limit", which shows a weight in tonnes in a red ring.

sku-002.s: You pass this combination of signs. What does the small sign at the bottom show?
a: The speed limit that applies on the enforcement section
The average speed of the traffic on the section
The length of the enforcement section in kilometres
The distance to the next camera
sku-002.f: The supplementary sign 856 \"Speed limit\" is placed under sign 556.2 \"Automatic traffic enforcement - average speed check\" and shows which speed limit applies on the enforcement section (skiltforskriften § 18 B.IV). Average speed enforcement calculates your average speed between two camera points, so it does not help to brake just before the second camera - you have to stay below the limit the whole way. The supplementary sign says nothing about how long the section is or where the next camera stands.

th-010.s: You have hitched up a trailer and are about to overtake a slow-moving car. What must you expect?
a: You need a considerably longer stretch than without a trailer
The overtaking takes just as little time as without a trailer
You may exceed the speed limit while the overtaking is in progress
Overtaking with a trailer is prohibited on a two-lane road
th-010.f: The combination is both longer and heavier, and both of these lengthen the overtaking: you take longer to build up speed, and you must drive further before the whole combination is clear of the car you are passing and you can pull back in. At the same time your speed is capped at the top. On stretches of road with a speed limit higher than 80 km/h, a motor vehicle with a trailer must not be driven faster than 80 km/h (the Traffic Rules section 13 no. 4), and there is no exception that lets you exceed the speed limit because you are in the middle of an overtaking. Expect a longer braking distance as well, and a greater need for space at junctions and roundabouts. If you are in doubt whether you will get past, the answer is to stay behind: overtaking with a trailer requires far more clear road than you are used to without one.

vp-014.s: You are driving on a priority road. What does that mean for you?
a: Crossing traffic must give way to you until the priority road ends
You may hold a higher speed than the signposted speed limit
Crossing traffic must give way - but only up to the first junction
The right-hand rule still applies at the small junctions along the way
vp-014.f: The sign is 206 "Priority road". It states that drivers coming from a side road or a crossing road are given a duty to give way by sign 202 "Give way" or 204 "Stop" (the Sign Regulations section 6). The priority road applies until it is revoked - by sign 208 "End of priority road", or by Give way or Stop being put up on your own road. It therefore does not end at the first junction, and the right-hand rule does not apply at the junctions along the way, not even the small ones. Two things right of way does not give you: it never changes the speed limit, and it does not release you from the duty of care. You must still expect someone to breach their duty to give way, especially at junctions with poor visibility and where the side road comes down steeply.

sk-111.f: Skilt 552 «Estacionamiento» (Skiltforskriften §12 (De enkelte opplysningsskilt)). La señal indica que el estacionamiento está permitido en el lugar, siempre que el estacionamiento no sea contrario a las disposiciones de las normas de tráfico sobre parada o estacionamiento. Si la señal lleva la placa complementaria 828 «Extensión de la regulación de parada o estacionamiento», está permitido estacionar en la dirección indicada aunque el estacionamiento sea contrario a las disposiciones de las normas de tráfico sobre parada y estacionamiento. Si una placa complementaria indica que el estacionamiento está reservado a determinados grupos de vehículos o de usuarios de la vía, el estacionamiento está prohibido para los demás. Si la señal está colocada en un área especialmente delimitada o junto a ella, p. ej. un aparcamiento, la señal rige para toda el área. En caso contrario, la señal rige solo en el lado de la vía en el que está colocada. La señal rige entonces hasta el cruce más próximo o hasta una nueva señal Skilt 552 «Estacionamiento», Skilt 370 «Prohibido detenerse», Skilt 372 «Prohibido estacionar» o hasta el Skilt 376 «Zona de estacionamiento». Si una miniatura de la señal, en su caso con placa complementaria, está colocada en un parquímetro, el estacionamiento está permitido conforme a las reglas especiales sobre estacionamiento de pago. La señal rige entonces para la plaza de estacionamiento correspondiente sin tener en cuenta las disposiciones de las normas de tráfico sobre parada y estacionamiento.
